ai_assessment.method: Full direct English-to-Vietnamese comparison of all 1548 canonical passages and both titles. Separate subagent drafting from the original preceded review. A separate-context assessor (same model family, not shown the drafter’s notes or scores) read every pair first and reported six major and about forty-five minor findings with a pre-revision weighted score of 8.51; the drafter revised the text, re-read the changed passages and the whole target for naturalness, then assigned these final scores bound to the final byte hashes.
ai_assessment.limitations: The same AI system drafted, revised and assessed the work; the separate-context pass is correlated same-model feedback, not independent review or model diversity. No human literary reviewer, native-reader trial or measured reader demand is claimed. Existing Vietnamese translations were not consulted or collated. Scores are subjective and uncalibrated; missed errors may remain. Source clearance is separately recorded and is not granted by this review.

findings.explanation: Jose’s ‘của con’ made the lace frock hers instead of Laura’s; now ‘váy ren của Laura’.
‘Steep rise’ was rendered as a gentle slope; now ‘con dốc đứng’.
‘Not for a long time’ was reversed; corrected.
‘Wished to God he understood’ was garbled; corrected.
‘She’ is the stewardess but the draft said ‘bà’ (grandmother); now ‘nữ phục vụ’.
The fortune-teller’s customer, a woman, was addressed as ‘ông’ and told she would marry a red-haired man; corrected.
Jonathan’s speech continued outside the quotation marks after the speech tag; the quote now reopens.
Pip’s child-spelling ‘nemeral’ is normalised to ‘lục bảo’ in units 96 and 98, so the mispronunciation joke is lost.
Address to the dead man at the climax (‘cháu’) is debatable.

summary: Full assessment of all 1,548 English/Vietnamese passages: fifteen story titles and every paragraph. The first reviews scored 8.70, 8.375, 8.40 and 8.55 across four ranges and found six majors (a frock given to the wrong sister, a steep rise written as a slope, a reversed ‘not for a long time’, a garbled wish, a stewardess written as a grandmother, a woman addressed as ‘ông’); a round of fixes and fresh separate-context blind reviews then scored 8.80 (units 1–542, after one further broken-quotation major was fixed and re-reviewed), 8.80 (543–933), 8.80 (934–1308) and 8.88 (1309–1548) with no major or critical finding open. The final score is taken from the weakest range, 8.80 on the half-point scale, above the unchanged 8.6 threshold. A few minor points, such as Pip’s child-spelling ‘nemeral’ and an address form at the climax, remain open.
